unmet_needs: Lean mass / muscle loss with high-magnitude weight loss — incretin-driven 20-25% TBWL is accompanied by ~25-40% of weight lost coming from fat-free mass; this raises long-term sarcopenia / functional decline concerns especially in older adults. WS13 review (Drucker, NRDD 2025, p.641) elevates muscle/lean-mass preservation to a PRIMARY differentiation axis distinct from raw %TBWL: sarcopenic obesity carries 2-3x mortality risk vs obesity alone (Benz 2024). Three strategy buckets: (1) muscle-sparing mechanisms — bimagrumab (ActRII antagonist, Lilly), trevogrumab + garetosmab (myostatin/activin antagonists, Regeneron Ph2); (2) amylin co-agonism (cagrilintide, eloralintide, amycretin) hypothesised to drive more selective adipose loss; (3) GIPR-modulator hypothesis (MariTide antagonism vs tirzepatide agonism). Lean-mass-sparing assets (bimagrumab, apitegromab, eloralintide, enobosarm) are racing to address this but none yet approved. [WS13 framing, analyst-known, verify]

Pharmacogenomics of weight-loss response — inter-individual variability in GLP-1RA response is high. WS13 review (Drucker, NRDD 2025, p.640) cites German et al. (Nat Med 2025; 10,960-subject analysis) linking polygenic scores for body weight + T2D and missense variants in GLP-1R/GIPR signalling to differential weight-loss response and weight-regain. No clinically deployed PGx test yet — an open differentiation axis for next-gen developers and a real-world stratification opportunity. [WS13 review-cited, analyst-known, verify]

Weight regain after discontinuation — STEP-4 / SURMOUNT-4 show ~two-thirds of lost weight regained within 12 months of drug withdrawal. Chronic indefinite dosing is the current paradigm; no maintenance-only label or dose-down protocol exists. SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN, ATTAIN-MAINTAIN, eloralintide Ph3 target this gap.

Oral options with parity efficacy vs injectables — oral semaglutide 50 mg (OASIS-4) and orforglipron (ACHIEVE/ATTAIN) approach but have not matched injectable tirzepatide on %TBWL; oral compliance, bioavailability, and food-state requirements remain hurdles. Pfizer danuglipron and lotiglipron discontinued in 2023-2025 for hepatic safety.

Genetic / hypothalamic / syndromic obesity beyond MC4R-pathway — setmelanotide is approved for POMC/LEPR/BBS/hypothalamic obesity but represents a small fraction of monogenic / syndromic patients; LB54640 (oral MC4R), bivamelagon, and pathway-adjacent assets are still early. Prader-Willi outcomes remain unsatisfactory.

GI tolerability and treatment discontinuation — nausea, vomiting, diarrhea drive ~5-10% discontinuation in pivotal trials and likely 20-30% real-world; titration regimens and improved tolerability profile (e.g., monthly MariTide) are an active design vector. Pancreatitis, gallbladder, and ileus signals remain under surveillance.

Adolescent and pediatric coverage — only semaglutide (STEP-TEENS, 12+), liraglutide, tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-Adol underway), and phentermine/topiramate ER (Qsymia, 2022) have adolescent labels; <12 yr remains largely off-label. Ethical and growth-trajectory considerations limit trials.

Reimbursement and access in non-diabetic obesity — US Medicare statutory carve-out (1965 SSA) still excludes weight-loss drugs (carve-out partial reform under MEPA pending Congress as of 2025); commercial PBM restrictions, prior auth, step-edit policies, and shortage-driven coverage cuts (Lilly Mounjaro, Wegovy 2023-2024) constrain real-world utilisation. Cash-pay & compounded-GLP-1 markets are filling some of the gap but raise quality/safety concerns.

Head-to-head comparative data — SURMOUNT-5 (tirzepatide vs semaglutide, NEJM 2025, PMID 40353578, NCT05822830) is the first published registrational H2H: tirzepatide -20.2% vs semaglutide -13.7% mean TBWL at w72 (superiority met). REDEFINE-T2 (CagriSema vs Zepbound) is ongoing. Beyond these two, the field still relies on cross-trial comparison — decision-grade comparative effectiveness across the dual / triple / amylin classes remains largely missing.

Cardiovascular outcomes for non-GLP-1 mechanisms — only semaglutide (SELECT) has a positive CVOT in obesity (no T2D). Tirzepatide SURPASS-CVOT (T2D) and SURMOUNT-MMO (obesity) are pending; for triple/dual/amylin/MC4R mechanisms, CVOTs do not yet exist — limits payer + guideline-led positioning vs semaglutide.

Body composition / VAT / cardiometabolic substudies are inconsistent — many pivotals do not report DEXA/MRI sub-analyses, making it hard to compare assets on visceral fat reduction, ectopic fat (liver, pancreas), or cardiac steatosis. Standardised composition endpoints needed across the class.

dual_agonist_general_obesity.surmount5_design_note: SURMOUNT-5 (tirzepatide -20.2% w72) is a SEPARATE trial from the -20.9% SURMOUNT-1 anchor and is NOT the same figure — do not pool or quote interchangeably. SURMOUNT-1 is the placebo-controlled registrational trial (tirzepatide 15 mg vs placebo); SURMOUNT-5 is an open-label active-comparator head-to-head (tirzepatide max-tolerated dose vs semaglutide 2.4 mg), both at w72. The two ~20% values corroborate the dual-incretin ceiling under different designs; SURMOUNT-5's contribution is the H2H delta of -6.5 pp vs semaglutide (superiority met). The -20.9% SURMOUNT-1 number remains the registrational anchor and is retained unchanged.
dual_agonist_general_obesity.incumbent_pressure_caveat: This ~20% dual-incretin TBWL is the incumbent SoC bar, not a ceiling. The pipeline is actively pressuring it and some entrants may clear it: DATA-BACKED today — retatrutide triple-G (TRIUMPH-1 Phase 3, -25.0% 12 mg w80 / -30.3% w104 BMI>=35 extension) exceeds the dual-incretin bar on CROSS-TRIAL comparison (no head-to-head vs tirzepatide yet). PENDING DATA — CagriSema (REDEFINE-T2 H2H vs Zepbound), maridebart cafraglutide (MariTide Phase 3, monthly dosing), and amylin/incretin combos (petrelintide+enicepatide) could also compete on efficacy and/or tolerability/convenience, but lack registrational or H2H data to confirm a win. novel_targets.evidence_summary: Male DIO mice: ZT0 BAY2402234 reduced weight gain, adiposity, hepatic TG + improved glucose tolerance; NO food intake change. Mechanism: restoration of daily mitochondrial redox oscillations disrupted by HFD.
